# pretest 1.0.4

TLS findings now name the reason instead of printing openssl noise.

`self-signed.badssl.com` was reported as "TLS-handskakning misslyckas" with 300
characters of s_client output as evidence. It now reads:

```
[HIGH] Certifikatet validerar inte: certifikatet är självsignerat
       bevis: Verify return code: 18 (self-signed certificate)
```

Same for expired, hostname mismatch and unavailable CA — and a handshake that the
server aborts says so ("servern stängde anslutningen under handskakningen") rather
than implying a certificate problem.

## Install

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/install.sh | bash
```

Installs `~/.local/bin/pretest` and verifies the checksum. Or take the file:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py -o pretest.py
curl -fsSL https://github.com/alexwest1981/pretest/releases/latest/download/pretest.py.sha256 | sha256sum -c -
chmod +x pretest.py
```

## Use

```bash
pretest --url https://example.com
pretest --url https://example.com --domain example.com --repo ~/code/app
pretest --url https://app.example.com -H "Cookie: session=…"   # behind a login
pretest --url https://example.com --fail-on high               # CI gate, exit 1
pretest --self-test                                            # verify the tool
```

Exposed artefacts, transport and TLS, header hygiene, cookie flags, CORS,
SPF/DMARC/DKIM/CAA, subdomains via crt.sh with dangling-CNAME takeover detection,
20 common ports, secrets in source, and dependency CVEs through `npm audit` /
`pip-audit` / `cargo audit` when installed. Anything it could not check is
reported as `info` — it never goes quiet.

## Limits

Not a pentest: no IDOR, no business logic, no injections in your own parameters.
Report text is Swedish, every finding has a stable English `id` in the JSON.
TLS 1.0/1.1 show as *untested* on a modern OpenSSL, not as unsupported. Port
findings behind a CDN describe the CDN edge and say so.
